items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: catch Debussy either. It had a different feeling than it does today.

ctx.x: Did you see or hear anything notable?

Only collecting an ambiance, certainly a feeling and I get that feeling every time I listen to Stravinsky of that period or Ravel in that period. It doesn't take too much imagination to go back a few years and catch Debussy either. It had a different feeling than it does today. New York had a different feeling. How do you describe that? I don't know. Europe was always a difficult place, I'm sure it was, but it also had more peripheral dimensions than it does now. It was impersonal, but not so impersonal. There…
You almost think of Europe as an entity anymore.
